title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook consolidates the end-to-end enterprise onboarding process for Redwood customers, including integration checklist, escalation playbook, known issues & workarounds, the ongoing support process, routine health checks, and QBR preparation guidance. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and any engineering owners who participate in enterprise onboarding and post-go-live operations.

Scope:
- New enterprise customers migrating from evaluation to production (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments)
- Major feature rollouts with customer-impacting migrations (model pinning, quantization changes, routing policy updates)
- Standardized playbook for go-live readiness and post-go-live operations for first 90 days

Owner & RACI:
- Document owner: Customer Success (Daniel Kim)
- Primary: Customer Success (Onboarding CSM), Solutions Engineering (Integration SE)
- Secondary: Eng-Platform, Eng-SRE, Eng-Serving-Runtime
- RACI (high level):
  - Responsible: Onboarding CSM, Integration SE
  - Accountable: Head of Customer Success
  - Consulted: Eng-SRE, Eng-Serving-Runtime, Security & Compliance
  - Informed: Sales, Product, Support

Prerequisites (before technical onboarding begins):
1. Signed contract and customer information captured in CRM (owner, billing contact, network owners)
2. Designated customer technical POC and weekly sync cadence established
3. Security questionnaires completed (if Private/Dedicated) and any network/VPC peering approved
4. Baseline usage profile: expected requests per minute, typical sequence length, latency targets, and traffic patterns (burst vs steady)

Onboarding Phases and Checklist:

Phase 0 - Pre-Onboarding (CSM lead)
- Confirm contract and entitlements (Dedicated capacity, Private deployment options).
- Kickoff call agenda: goals, timeline, success criteria, risk areas (PII/regulatory concerns, throughput targets).
- Deliverables: Onboarding plan, contact matrix, slack channel or equivalent for day-to-day comms.

Phase 1 - Integration & Technical Setup (SE lead)
- Integration checklist:
  - API keys and access created; customer verifies calls against Redwood Sandbox.
  - Network connectivity configured: for Hosted - IP allowlist; for Private - VPN/VPC peering and KMS setup.
  - Model selection & pinning: customer chooses model family and pins default model/version for initial rollout.
  - Rate limits & quotas set based on contract.
  - Logging and audit collection enabled (audit-logging integration verified).
  - Observability hooks: route-level metrics, tracing enabled, ingestion to customer or Redwood dashboards as agreed.
- Integration SE delivers a minimal example app and an API smoke test script. Example curl: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \\
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1x", "prompt":"Hello"}'

Phase 2 - Scale Testing & Performance Validation (Eng-SRE/SE)
- Run load tests that mirror the stated customer traffic profile.
- Validate SLOs and thresholds:
  - Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for chat endpoints; p99 <= 800ms (hosted; dedicated/private SLOs may vary)
  - Error rate: combined 4xx/5xx < 1% during steady-state testing
  - Throughput validated to sustained RPS and burst capacity validated to contracted burst levels
- Monitor KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency. Record baseline token costs per 1k tokens.

Phase 3 - Go-Live & Stabilization (CSM + SE + Eng-SRE)
- Go/no-go checklist (all must be green):
  1. Integration tests pass in customer environment.
  2. Load and scaling tests meet agreed SLOs.
  3. Observability dashboards configured and alerts created.
  4. Escalation contacts & on-call rotation for first 72 hours confirmed.
  5. Rollout policy configured in Console (canary/baseline/auto-fallback).
- Post go-live stabilization window: 0-72 hours critical monitoring with SE and Eng-SRE in-together. Daily sync for first week; weekly thereafter for 90 days.

Escalation Playbook (technical incidents during onboarding and first 90 days)

Purpose: Provide deterministic steps for severity classification, immediate mitigation, and escalation paths.

Severity definitions:
- Sev 1 (Critical): Customer production traffic impacted (major outage or data loss), no workaround, high business impact.
- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation in performance (latency or errors) for a subset of requests or customers; workaround exists but reduces functionality or increases cost significantly.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional issues with limited impact, non-critical features affected.
- Sev 4 (Low): Cosmetic issues, documentation requests, or feature clarifications.

Immediate incident steps (all severities):
1. Triage: Triage in shared channel, collect request IDs, timestamps, sample payloads, and top-level logs.
2. Scope: Determine blast radius (single customer, subset of routes, or platform-wide).
3. Mitigate: If possible, apply immediate mitigation (route fallback to compatible model variant, increase capacity for Dedicated customers, or temporarily switch to lower-precision quantized model to reduce memory pressure).
4. Escalate: Use the contact matrix below depending on severity.

Contact & escalation matrix:
- Sev 1: On-call Eng-SRE (pager) -> Eng-Serving-Runtime senior engineer -> Head of Engineering on call -> Customer Exec escalation (if >4 hours unresolved).
- Sev 2: Support Engineering -> Eng-Serving-Runtime primary owner -> On-call Eng-SRE (if resource constraint suspected).
- Sev 3: Support queue -> Solutions Engineering -> Product (for non-prod feature/config issues).

Required incident artifacts to attach to ticket:
- Repro steps and smallest possible payload to reproduce
- Request IDs and timestamp range
- Relevant logs (gateway, runtime, model backend) and metric graphs for the relevant time window
- Recent config changes or model rollouts in last 24-72 hours

Escalation playbook example (Sev 1):
1. Acknowledge within 15 minutes.
2. Triage and capture blast radius in 30 minutes.
3. If mitigation not found within 60 minutes, escalate to Eng-Serving-Runtime and Eng-SRE leads.
4. Determine rollback or fallback strategy (e.g., pin to previous stable model version) and execute after engineering approval.
5. Communicate to customer with hourly updates until resolved.

Integration Guides & Common Setup Patterns
- Hosted: API key management, request signing (if used), and IP allowlist instructions.
- Dedicated: capacity reservation verification, autoscaling policy attachments, and burst settings.
- Private: VPC peering checklist, KMS/HSM integration steps, air-gapped packaging notes.

Sample network checklist (Private deployments):
| Item | Required | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| VPC CIDR | yes | Confirm non-overlapping with Redwood peer network |
| BGP | optional | Only for cross-region hybrid set-ups |
| Allowed egress to Redwood control plane | yes | Ports 443 and 5222 for metrics/heartbeat |
| KMS integration | yes | Provide key ARN and rotation policy |

Known Issues & Workarounds (common during onboarding)
- High p99 latency for long-context requests: Workaround - reduce batch window for long sequences or split requests into smaller context windows; consider enabling KV cache for repeated prefix tokens.
- Memory OOMs on Private/dedicated nodes after model quantization: Workaround - revert to FP16 for the faulting model variant, increase reserved GPU memory for that pool, and open support ticket to investigate kernel selection.
- Sudden spike of 429s during burst: Workaround - temporarily raise route-specific quota for customer or apply burst queue increase; configure graceful retry at client side with exponential backoff.
- Misaligned embeddings between versions (embedding drift): Workaround - pin embedding model version at client side and re-run small migration to re-index critical vectors.

Support Process, SLAs & Escalation SLAs
- Standard support channels: support@redwood.ai, dedicated Slack channel, ticketing via Zendesk (enterprise queue).
- Response SLAs (during onboarding window):
  - Sev 1: Ack within 15 minutes, initial engineering response within 60 minutes.
  - Sev 2: Ack within 30 minutes, initial response within 4 hours.
  - Sev 3: Ack within 4 business hours, initial response within 24 hours.
  - Sev 4: Response in 3 business days.
- Business hours defined per contract (24x7 for enterprise with premium SLA).
- Escalation cadence: hourly updates for Sev 1 until resolved, 4-hour cadence for Sev 2, daily for Sev 3.

Health Checks & QBR materials
- 7/30/90 day health checks (templates below):
  - 7-day: Verify integration, error rate, initial token usage, and any immediate issues.
  - 30-day: Performance baseline, cost-per-token analysis, prompt/response quality review, and tuning recommendations (batching, caching, quantization).
  - 90-day: Business outcomes review, cost optimization report, roadmap alignment, and longer-term scaling plan.

QBR template (recommended slides/sections):
1. Executive summary (health status: Green/Yellow/Red)
2. Usage & growth trends (tokens/month, requests/day, average sequence length)
3. Performance metrics (p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, availability)
4. Cost breakdown (tokens, model selection, reserved vs burst costs, recommendations)
5. Quality & regressions (evals, sample prompts, user feedback)
6. Action items & owners (next 90-day plan)

Operational dashboards to include for QBR:
- Route-level latency and error rate timeseries
- Token consumption by model and route
- KV cache hit rate and batching statistics
- Alerts and incidents in last 90 days (with resolution times)

Templates & Example Artifacts
- 7/30/90 checklist (CSV attachable): columns [check,owner,due,date_completed,notes]
- Sample smoke-test script (bash) and loadtest configuration (k6 JSON) attached to this page in the artifacts section.

Post-Onboarding Handoff & Continuous Improvement
- Handoff checklist: all runbooks transferred to customer, long-term contacts updated, retention policy and compliance artifacts delivered.
- Quarterly reviews: schedule QBRs and share playbook changes.
- Feedback loop: Issues discovered during onboarding should be logged to the onboarding-feedback tracker and triaged monthly with Eng-Platform and Eng-Serving-Runtime for product/operational improvements.

Appendices
A. Quick rollback commands (example for model pin rollback via Redwood Console API):
  PATCH /api/projects/{project_id}/routes/{route_id}
  {"model_pin": "redwood-1x@v2026-02-10"}

B. Common observability queries (example PromQL):
  sum(rate(redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route)

C. Onboarding artifacts & attachments:
- smoke-test.sh (bash)
- k6-loadtest.json
- onboarding-checklist.csv

If you have questions about any section of this playbook or need help tailoring it for a specific customer deployment (Dedicated or Private), please contact the owner or post in #cs-onboarding (internal).
